useCase.name: Record when staff arrive and leave, and correct a wrong record under approval

intent.name: staff.attendance.mark
intent.summary: Record a staff member's day — when they arrived and how the day is coded. One step, and payroll reads the code.
routesHere: mark Miss Nadia present today, in at 07:50

routesHere.text: Miss Nadia ki hazri laga do, subah 7:50 pe aayi thin
routesHere.gloss: mark Miss Nadia's attendance, she came at 7:50

routesHere.text: Mr Asif aaj chhutti pe hain
routesHere.gloss: Mr Asif is on leave today

routesHere.text: device kaam nahi kar raha, haath se hazri laga do
routesHere.gloss: the device is not working, mark attendance by hand

routesHere: record this staff member as absent for yesterday

request.gloss: the attendance needs correcting

routesElsewhere.note: A record already made is corrected under the Principal's approval, not marked again (BR-7).

request.gloss: record the time out

routesElsewhere.note: The time in and the time out are entered at different moments (BR-2).

request.gloss: mark my own attendance

routesElsewhere.goesTo: Not offered to a School Admin.
routesElsewhere.note: The School Admin's own attendance is marked by the Principal — the person who marks should not be the person who marks themselves (BR-5, E1).

request.gloss: attendance is marked by card

routesElsewhere.note: Where a staff member has forgotten their card, the code-verified route applies. A scan itself is not planned.

steps.note: One step. Every day is coded, because payroll reads the code and an uncoded day is a day nobody can be paid for (BR-3, E2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Marking one's own record, an uncoded day and a future date are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the record with its code, its time in and the audit entry together or not at all. The code drives the month's payable days, derived from the codes rather than entered separately (BR-11). A day off or a holiday is coded as such and never counted as an absence (BR-8); a day on approved leave is coded Leave, not Absent, because payroll and any disciplinary process treat the two differently (BR-9).

parameters.type: enum: Present | Absent | Leave | Day-off | Holiday
parameters.notes: How the day is treated. Payroll reads it (BR-3), so an uncoded day is a day nobody can be paid for. Leave and Absent are different facts (BR-9); Day-off and Holiday come from the calendar (BR-8).

parameters.name: time_in
parameters.notes: When they arrived, in 24-hour form. Required in substance where the code is Present.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: leave_code_applied

errors.meaning: The School Admin attempted to mark their own attendance.
errors.note: Message: "Your own attendance is marked by the Principal." The person who marks should not mark themselves (BR-5).
Payroll reads the code, and an uncoded day is a day nobody can be paid for (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The date is in the future.
Accounts attempted to set a code.
errors.note: The role that calculates pay must not be the role that sets the days it is calculated from (BR-10).

errors.meaning: A Super Admin attempted to mark a record.
errors.note: A technical administrator is not a person who decides what somebody is paid (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the code. Payroll reads it (BR-3), so a code a planner picked decides what somebody is paid — and Absent, Leave, Day-off and Holiday are four different statements about one day.

Never code a day Absent where leave or the calendar applies. A day on approved leave is coded Leave and a closed day is coded as closed, and both are treated differently by payroll and by any disciplinary process (BR-8, BR-9).
Never mark the acting user's own record. E1 is BR-5 working — the School Admin's attendance is the Principal's to mark.
Never supply a time in the actor did not state. A time somebody entered is not evidence of when they arrived (UC-05-06 BR-3), and it sits on a record that determines pay.
Never mark a staff member on Accounts' or a Super Admin's behalf. Accounts read the record for payroll and cannot amend it (BR-10); a Super Admin holds no authority over it at all (BR-12).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A recorded day is not re-marked. It is corrected through staff.attendance.correction.raise, which takes effect only when the Principal approves it (BR-7), and the original entry stays visible alongside the corrected one (BR-13). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

errors.meaning: The time out is earlier than the time in.

planningRules.rule: Never supply a time out the actor did not state. A missing time out does not invalidate the day (BR-4), and a guessed departure sits on a record that determines pay.
Never swap the times to get past E10. A time out before a time in means one of the two is wrong, and which is a question for the person who observed it.
Never treat a blank time out as a problem to fix. It is explicitly permitted, and the gap is visible rather than guessed at (BR-4).
Never let a time out change the day's code. The code is what payroll reads (BR-3), and it is set when the day is marked.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing reason, an attempt by Accounts, and a month already sent to payroll are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors or as flagged outcomes.

operations.name: staff.attendance.correction.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: staff_id + date + corrected_code, since a day carries one pending correction at a time
operations.purpose: Raise a correction to a staff attendance record for the Principal to approve.

parameters.name: staff_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active staff member matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with department and role.

parameters.notes: The staff member, resolved from how the actor named them.

parameters.name: date
parameters.notes: The day whose record is wrong.

parameters.name: corrected_code
parameters.type: enum: Present | Absent | Leave | Day-off | Holiday
parameters.notes: What the code should be. Read from what the actor stated — the four codes are four different statements about a day, and payroll reads whichever is approved.

parameters.name: correction_reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. Mandatory, since this record determines pay and a change to it with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first (BR-6, E4). The actor's own words.

parameters.name: corrected_time_in
parameters.notes: Where the time is what was wrong.

parameters.name: corrected_time_out
parameters.notes: Where the departure was wrong.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: correction_id
fields.description: The correction.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Correction pending. The record is unchanged.

fields.name: current_code
fields.description: What the record says now, and what payroll still reads.

fields.name: corrected_code
fields.description: What it would become.

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not also approve it (BR-7, E6).

fields.name: sent_to_payroll
fields.description: True where the month has already gone to payroll (E9). The correction is handled differently and the message says so.

fields.name: payable_days_effect
fields.description: What the change would do to the month's payable days (BR-11).

errors.meaning: A correction was raised with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason. This record determines pay." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to change a code.
errors.note: The role that calculates pay must not be the role that sets the days it is calculated from (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The month has already been sent to payroll.
errors.notWritten: The month's figure is not changed by it.
errors.note: Reported rather than refused. Somebody has to decide how it is handled, and the message says so.

errors.meaning: A Super Admin attempted a correction.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the correction reason. This record determines pay, and a change to it with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first (BR-6).
Never choose the corrected code. Present, Absent, Leave, Day-off and Holiday are five different statements about one day, and payroll reads whichever is approved.
Never chain the approval. The School Admin raises it; they do not grant it (BR-7), and a correction to a pay record approved by the person who raised it is not a control.
Report the effect on the month's payable days. They are derived from the codes (BR-11), and a correction that moves a day from Absent to Present moves somebody's pay.
Report MONTH_SENT_TO_PAYROLL rather than treating it as a refusal. The correction is raised and somebody has to decide how it is handled (E9) — a month already paid is not corrected silently.

reversal.statement: A raised correction is approved or rejected by the Principal; nothing here withdraws one. The record is unchanged and payroll still reads the original code meanwhile.

parameters.name: branch_id
